info.name: Credential-service
info.description:
Manual test collection for the credential-service Go API.

Set the `base_url` variable if the service isn't running on the default localhost:8081.

Credential types: PAN, GST, FSSAI, UDYAM are all defined declaratively as YAML files under `configs/credential-types/*.yaml` (loaded once at process start into a VerifierRegistry). They resolve on both `/verify` and `/credential` — the two endpoints share one registry, and `/verify` has no per-type restriction, so anything with a YAML definition is reachable from either endpoint. `PAN_TO_GST` is the one credential type from the original design doc that was never implemented (no YAML file, no enum row) — it's the collection's example of a genuinely unsupported cred_type. Adding a new credential type is a config change (drop a new `<TYPE>.vN.yaml` in that directory), not a code change.

Validation is field-based (`validation.fields` in each YAML — see configs/credential-types/README.md) and presence-only: each cred_data key can declare `required`, checked after normalization/trim — there is no format/regex validation. Right now only `id_no` is required for any of the four types, so `cred_id` + `cred_type` is the complete request body everywhere — `name`/`dob` are accepted but not required or sent to any provider for any type (PAN included).

Each credential type also lists an ordered `providers` chain (`configs/credential-types/*.yaml`) — a transport error or a failed result from one provider falls through to the next. PAN lists `digio` then a deterministic `mock` fallback so the chain is exercisable without a second real vendor; GST/FSSAI/UDYAM currently list `digio` only. Both `/verify` and `/credential`'s results report which provider actually produced the result (`provider` in the response), and only include the provider's raw response body (`provider_response`) when the request is made with `?verbose=true`.

## Signature auth (security header validation) — ON by default in this collection

`/verify` and `/credential` are protected by an ONDC-style Ed25519 Authorization header when the server has `CREDENTIAL_SERVICE_AUTH_ENABLED=true` — only the registry service is meant to call these, never an NP directly. This collection's `auth_enabled` variable defaults to `true` and every request below is auto-signed by a collection-level pre-request script accordingly. For this to actually pass against your server, run it with matching env vars:

```
CREDENTIAL_SERVICE_AUTH_ENABLED=true
CREDENTIAL_SERVICE_AUTH_REGISTRY_SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY=AAKcVCZkFN4nO6UMzGVMoU0NaK2DuAT9d492gqzld3c=
CREDENTIAL_SERVICE_AUTH_REGISTRY_SUBSCRIBER_ID=registry.local.test
CREDENTIAL_SERVICE_AUTH_REGISTRY_UNIQUE_KEY_ID=registry-key-1
```

(the public key above matches the throwaway `registry_private_key` already filled into this collection's `registry_private_key` / `subscriber_id` / `unique_key_id` variables — do NOT reuse this keypair anywhere real). If your server is running with `CREDENTIAL_SERVICE_AUTH_ENABLED=false` (the `.env.sample` default), the signed header is harmless — the middleware is a no-op and ignores it — but you'll be testing the unauthenticated path, not the auth layer. To go back to unauthenticated testing, set the collection variable `auth_enabled` to `false`.

The signing happens in a collection-level pre-request script (Ed25519 sign + BLAKE2b-512 digest implemented in pure JS, verified byte-for-byte against this repo's own `pkg/ondcauth` Go implementation) — it runs before every request and adds the `Authorization` header whenever `auth_enabled` is `true`, skipping `/health` which is never protected. See the "Signature Auth" folder for explicit positive/negative examples (deliberately-broken headers, so those still 401 even with a correctly-configured server). You can also generate a header manually via `go run ./scripts/signreq -private-key ... -body '...'` if you prefer a CLI (e.g. for curl).

variable.description: Required by every POST /credential request (SubmitCredentialsRequest.ParticipantID, validate:"required"). Placeholder value — this field is validated but not currently persisted or otherwise used downstream.

Defaults to 'true': this collection signs every request with an ONDC Authorization header. Must match the server's CREDENTIAL_SERVICE_AUTH_ENABLED — set to 'false' here to test the unauthenticated path instead.

Base64 Ed25519 private key used to sign requests when auth_enabled=true. This is a throwaway local-testing keypair generated for this collection — do not use it for anything real. Its matching public key (for the server's CREDENTIAL_SERVICE_AUTH_REGISTRY_SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY) is AAKcVCZkFN4nO6UMzGVMoU0NaK2DuAT9d492gqzld3c=.
keyId subscriber_id segment. Only enforced server-side if CREDENTIAL_SERVICE_AUTH_REGISTRY_SUBSCRIBER_ID is set.
keyId unique_key_id segment. Only enforced server-side if CREDENTIAL_SERVICE_AUTH_REGISTRY_UNIQUE_KEY_ID is set.
A second, unrelated throwaway Ed25519 private key — used only by the "Invalid Signature - Wrong Key" example to prove the server rejects a validly-shaped but wrong signature.

request.description:
Synchronous verification. Returns a structured envelope — `{success, provider, cred_id, data, error}` — instead of the raw provider response; `provider` names whichever provider (from PAN.v1.yaml's ordered `providers` list) actually produced the result. Add `?verbose=true` to also include the provider's raw response body as `provider_response`.

PAN.v1.yaml lists `digio` then a deterministic `mock` fallback: this sample PAN is only valid in shape and Digio's sandbox will reject it (`{"code":"BAD_REQUEST","message":"Invalid Pan Number Detected"}`) — so as sent, this request demonstrates the fallback chain live: Digio rejects, the service automatically retries via `mock`, and you get back `success:true, "provider":"mock"`. GST/FSSAI/UDYAM have no fallback configured, so the same kind of provider-side rejection on those types returns `success:false` with `provider` set to whichever single provider ran.

Only a real transport failure (all configured providers unreachable) returns a 502 from this API. PAN uses cred_id + cred_type only (same shape as GST/FSSAI/UDYAM) — name/dob are not sent to any provider.

If the collection variable `auth_enabled` is `true`, this request is auto-signed by the collection's pre-request script — see the top-level collection description and the "Signature Auth" folder.

Same as "Verify PAN" but with `?verbose=true` enabled, so the response additionally includes `provider_response` — the exact raw JSON body returned by whichever provider (`digio` or, after fallback, `mock`) produced the result.

cred_id must match the pattern declared in configs/credential-types/FSSAI.v1.yaml (14 digits). Hits Digio's `/client/v4/apis/kyc/fetch_id_data/FSSAI` endpoint — a different base path than PAN/GST's v3 endpoint. The YAML declares `provider.capability: fetch_id_data_fssai`, which resolves to that path via configs/providers/digio.v1.yaml's capability catalog (not a raw path in the credential-type YAML itself). This sample id is only valid in shape (borrowed from a real Digio response example, not a live license) — expect Digio to reject it (still HTTP 200 from this API; the response body is Digio's own error verbatim).

cred_id accepts either the canonical hyphenated form shown here (UDYAM-XX-00-0000000) or the compact form with no separators (e.g. UDYAMMH011234567) — both are normalized to the hyphenated form (per configs/credential-types/UDYAM.v1.yaml's `normalization`) before being sent to Digio. Hits `/client/v4/apis/kyc/fetch_id_data/UDYAMAADHAAR`. This sample id is only valid in shape, not a live registration — expect a Digio-side rejection (still HTTP 200 here). Digio is documented to flap on this endpoint (the same valid Udyam number sometimes 200s with no data); the async `/credential` path retries automatically on that, but this synchronous endpoint does not.
Expect 400 {"error":"cred_id is required"}
Expect 400 {"error":"cred_type is required"}.

Expect 400 {"error":"unsupported credential type: PAN_TO_GST"}. PAN_TO_GST is named in the original design doc but was never implemented — there is no `configs/credential-types/PAN_TO_GST.v1.yaml` and no enum row, so the config-driven registry never registers a verifier for it. Any cred_type without a matching YAML file in `configs/credential-types/` produces this same error (try "AADHAAR" for another example).

item.name: Verify PAN - Format no longer validated (200, regex removed)

request.description: Regex format validation was removed from `validation.fields` (POC feedback) — only `required` (presence) is checked now. A format-invalid but present cred_id like this one used to 400 before any provider call; it now reaches the provider chain like any other value. Digio's real sandbox will reject this shape too, so — same as the default "Verify PAN" request — expect this to fall back to the `mock` provider and return `success:true, "provider":"mock"`.

Flat request shape per the design doc's Credential API (participant_id at the top level, plus cred_type/cred_id per credential — no nested cred_data). participant_id is required by SubmitCredentialsRequest's validate tag (internal/handlers/dto/credential_request.go) but is not currently persisted or otherwise used past that check — it's validated and then discarded. PAN uses cred_id + cred_type only; name/dob are not required for any type. Paste the response's request_id into the {{request_id}} collection variable to use with "Get Credential Results" below.

cred_id must be 14 digits (configs/credential-types/FSSAI.v1.yaml). Endpoint/response shapes sourced from team_pipeline_2807.py's verify_fssai(), not the design doc. Digio returns one of two response shapes for FSSAI; both are handled. This sample id is shape-valid only, not a live license — check GET /credential afterwards to see the worker's actual result (likely FAILED against the real Digio sandbox).

cred_id accepts either the canonical hyphenated form shown here or the compact form (e.g. UDYAMMH011234567) — normalized before reaching Digio. Digio is documented to flap on this endpoint (a valid Udyam number sometimes 200s with no data) — this async path is the reason that flakiness is tolerable at all: a 200-with-no-UAN response is treated as a soft failure and retried automatically (up to max_retries), unlike the synchronous /verify endpoint. This sample id is shape-valid only, not a live registration.

item.name: Submit Credentials - Multiple in one batch (all 4 types)

request.description: Each credential in the batch is processed independently — one item's failure or retry doesn't affect the others. Response echoes cred_id per item so same-type duplicates in a batch stay distinguishable. Paste the request_id into {{request_id}} and use "Get Credential Results" to see all four outcomes.
Missing cred_type should fail dto validation before ever reaching the DB.

Expect 400 — PAN_TO_GST has no YAML definition under configs/credential-types/ (named in the original design doc, never implemented; see Implementation Status in Credential Service Implementation Plan.md). Rejected during SubmitCredentials' pre-persistence validation, before anything is written to credential_requests.
Expect 400 {"error":"cred_id is required"} — validated by dto struct tags before ever reaching the service/DB.

Expect 400 {"error":"ParticipantID is required"} (utils.Validate's jsonFieldName() has no case for ParticipantID, so it falls back to the raw Go struct field name here rather than "participant_id" — unlike cred_id/cred_type/name/dob errors elsewhere in this collection).

Fetch the results of a previously submitted /credential request (paste the request_id from a Submit Credentials response into the {{request_id}} variable, or replace it inline). request_id is a query param, not a path segment. The response's `credentials` array echoes each submitted `cred_id` alongside our internal `id`, so multiple same-type credentials in one batch (e.g. two PANs) can still be told apart. Each item also reports `provider` — whichever provider in that credential type's fallback chain actually produced the result (e.g. `DIGIO` or, for PAN after a Digio rejection, `MOCK`). Add `?verbose=true` to also include that provider's raw response body as `provider_response` once the item is processed; without it, only the normalized fields above are returned. A still-PENDING item, or one whose failure never reached a provider, instead has `verification_errors` populated. 404 if the request_id doesn't exist, 400 if it's missing or not a valid UUID.
Expect 404 {"error":"credential request not found"}
Expect 400 {"error":"request_id is required"}

item.name: Signature Auth (security header validation)
item.description: Explicit positive/negative examples of the ONDC Ed25519 Authorization header enforced by internal/middleware/signature_auth.go when the server runs with CREDENTIAL_SERVICE_AUTH_ENABLED=true. Every request in this folder relies on the collection-level pre-request script to sign first, then a request-level pre-request script deliberately breaks the header to demonstrate a specific rejection reason (except the first, which is left untouched to show the happy path). If the server has CREDENTIAL_SERVICE_AUTH_ENABLED=false (the default), the middleware is a no-op and ALL of these will return 200/normal responses regardless of the header.

request.description: Signed by the collection-level pre-request script using registry_private_key/subscriber_id/unique_key_id, unmodified. With CREDENTIAL_SERVICE_AUTH_ENABLED=true and CREDENTIAL_SERVICE_AUTH_REGISTRY_SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY set to this collection's matching public key (AAKcVCZkFN4nO6UMzGVMoU0NaK2DuAT9d492gqzld3c=), expect the request to pass the auth layer entirely (no 401) — any error you see past that point comes from Digio/validation, not from signature auth.
Request-level script strips whatever Authorization header the collection script just set. With auth_enabled server-side, expect 401 {"error":"authorization header is required"}.

Request-level script re-signs the same body with wrong_private_key (a different, unrelated Ed25519 key) instead of registry_private_key, keeping the same keyId. The keyId parses fine but the signature does not verify against the server's configured public key. Expect 401 {"error":"invalid authorization header: invalid signature"}.

item.name: Unexpected Subscriber ID (401, only if pinned)

request.description: Request-level script re-signs with a different subscriber_id in the keyId, using the correct registry_private_key. This only fails if the server has CREDENTIAL_SERVICE_AUTH_REGISTRY_SUBSCRIBER_ID set to pin the expected identity — expect 401 {"error":"invalid authorization header: unexpected subscriber_id in keyId"} in that case. If the server leaves that variable unset (pinning disabled), this request passes auth like the "Valid Signature" example, since the signature itself is still valid.
